appraisal_events.evidence: l'amitié n'est pas seulement dénuée de vertu comme la conversation, elle est de plus funeste... Je me mentais à moi-même... quand je me félicitais d'être aimé, admiré, par un être aussi bon, aussi intelligent, aussi recherché que Saint-Loup... je m'efforçais de trouver une beauté... qui donnerait plus de mérite à Robert, à moi-même, à ma vie.
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator retrospectively exposes his earlier pleasure at being admired by Saint-Loup as self-deceiving vanity, judging friendship itself as sterile and even harmful next to solitary artistic pursuit, and so locally devalues the worth of Saint-Loup's regard even while still naming him good, intelligent, and sought-after.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator downgrades the significance of Saint-Loup's friendship and admiration, framing his earlier delight in it as illusory self-flattery, though Saint-Loup's personal qualities are not themselves attacked.

ambiguities: The diminishment is aimed chiefly at the value and sincerity of the narrator's own admiration for being befriended by Saint-Loup, rather than at Saint-Loup's personal qualities, which remain explicitly praised ('aussi bon, aussi intelligent, aussi recherché'); this self-directed irony could alternatively be read as centering on the narrator rather than on Saint-Loup.

The narrator's claim that Saint-Loup 'me jugea mal' (judged him badly) for declining the visit is presented as mere supposition ('sans doute') and is not confirmed, so it is not recorded as a separate event.
